privacy.heading: Privacy statement and terms of use
privacy.intro: Read this on first launch: where your data lives, when it leaves this machine, and under what conditions a resume actually gets sent.
privacy.keyPromise: The promise: your resume is never sent to an employer without your confirmation.
privacy.keyPromiseDetail: The default autonomy level is the most conservative one, and no outbound action runs on its own. Making it automatic takes two explicit choices from you - raise the level to automatic, and add that action to the auto-confirm list. The program cannot raise its own level, and the platform risk signature plus the daily quota gate still stand in front.
privacy.dataLocal: Resume text, knowledge base, job records, chat history, logs and screenshot evidence are all written into the app data directory on this machine (one database file plus an evidence folder). We have no cloud account and no feature that syncs your data to any server.
privacy.dataDir: Location: %APPDATA%\auto-cc on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/auto-cc on macOS, ~/.config/auto-cc on Linux.
privacy.dataKeptAfterUninstall: Uninstalling keeps that directory - your login state and knowledge base are your assets. To remove everything, quit the app and delete it yourself.
privacy.noTelemetry: No telemetry, no analytics, no usage tracking, no crash reporting.
privacy.netAutomation: Only after you enable automation for a platform does the built-in browser visit it, carrying your own login: searching jobs, reading details, greeting, delivering all happen inside that browser, and requests go to the platform itself.
privacy.netLlm: AI features (drafting messages, tailoring text to a job, semantic search) talk to the provider you configure yourself: requests happen only once you fill in the base URL and key, otherwise the feature just reports what is missing. When they do run they send the passage relevant to the current job, not the whole library.
privacy.netNoBackground: Beyond those two, there is no background network traffic: the UI, fonts and offline assets ship inside the app, so the main screen opens without any connection.
privacy.resumeTitle: When a resume actually goes out
privacy.resumeNeverAuto: That promise is a check in the code, not marketing: one outbound action must pass the autonomy level, the auto-confirm list, the quota gate and the platform risk signature, and it stops if any one of them is missing.
privacy.resumeApprovalChain: At the level that requires confirmation you get an approval card naming the job and the exact attachment. Denying it, or letting it time out, both end as "not delivered".
privacy.resumePauseAnytime: You can abort or take over at any point: the yield checkpoint sits before the send, so a paused step never hands the resume over.
privacy.riskPlatform: Script-driven searching, greeting and delivering can be flagged as abnormal behaviour by a recruiting platform. The consequences (warnings, rate limits, account bans) fall on the account being operated.
privacy.riskConsentCard: That is why every platform shows a separate risk confirmation card before its first action. That card answers "should this account be used"; this screen answers "where is the data" - both matter.
privacy.riskNoEvasion: This app does not solve captchas or work around platform defences: when either appears it stops and hands control back to you. Throttling and daily caps are mandatory, not optional.
privacy.termsSelfUse: This is a tool for your own job search: operate only accounts and material you have the right to use, and do not use it to mass-spam employers.
privacy.termsNoWarranty: The software is provided as is, with no guarantee of interviews or offers. You own the truthfulness of your resume - the app only assists with fact checking and will not invent experience for you.
privacy.termsUpdateChoice: Updates are your decision: the app does not download an installer for you in the background.
privacy.licensesPointer: Third-party licences are listed per package in LICENSES.md and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt inside the install directory, distributed with the app.

autonomy.section: How much the agent decides for you

why.suggest: It only writes the plan out for you; it runs nothing
why.semi: It reads pages on its own; anything that writes or sends asks you first
why.auto: Everything runs except the hands that send messages out

autonomy.compareToggle: What actually differs between the three

compare.suggest: On Suggest it does not even read a page: it only writes out what it plans to do. Start here if you want to see the arrangement first.
compare.semi: On Semi-auto the read-only hands run by themselves (search jobs, read details); anything that touches local files or sends something out stops for your confirmation.
compare.auto: On Full-auto everything runs except the hands that send messages out — those always ask unless you add them to the no-confirmation list below. Quota, throttling and daily caps apply on every tier.

gap.heading: Job gap report
gap.hint: Compares a pasted JD against your local knowledge base right now. The three columns are states — matched, partially matched, missing — and rows inside a column keep the extraction order; the panel never re-sorts. Counts, scores and states all come from the main process. When the model leg is unavailable the report falls back to the lexical baseline and is simply shorter. The three text thresholds were calibrated on 42 locally annotated samples (2026-10-02); the years ratio and the highlight cap are product decisions, and every value still lives in the kb-gap section of cordis.yml. The lexical ruler only sees literal overlap, so a differently worded but equivalent claim can read as missing.
gap.jdPlaceholder: Paste the JD body (the full description — a job title alone yields no requirements)
gap.stale: The knowledge base just changed, so the previous report's evidence is stale — press Compare gaps again.
gap.scoreDisplayOnly: the years row shows this score for reference only; its colour follows the state
gap.evidenceGone: This evidence is no longer in the library: the report is a stale reading, run the comparison again.
gap.libraryMissing: There is no knowledge base to compare against yet: import your résumé in the Library entities panel below and sync it, then come back. This is not “you do not qualify” — nothing was compared.
gap.noEntities: 0 entities in the library — every missing row here only says your résumé has not been entered yet, not that you are unqualified.
gap.noRequirements: This JD ({{chars}} characters) yielded no comparable requirements: the text is probably too short or is only a job title. Try a fuller description.

generate.heading: Tailor this résumé to a JD
generate.hint: Paste a JD: the main process reorders sections and entries by relevance, proposes rewrites on allowlisted fields, then runs the deterministic fact check over the result. What you get is a proposal — locked facts (company, role, period, degree) stay verbatim and no number may appear out of thin air. Only the rows you tick and then accept are written into the working copy.
generate.jdPlaceholder: Paste the JD body (the same text you feed the gap report)
generate.stale: The library or the working copy changed, so this proposal's baseline no longer holds: generate again before accepting.
generate.outcomeRewritten: {{count}} rewrite(s) proposed: review each row, tick it, and only then does accept write it into the working copy
generate.outcomeReorderOnly: No rewrite was adopted; {{moves}} position(s) were re-ordered by relevance (conservative output — the feature does not degrade to unavailable)
generate.outcomeRejected: The fact check failed ({{count}} violation(s)), so this run produced nothing: there is no document to accept
generate.modelMerged: Model leg answered through {{model}}; {{dropped}} row(s) dropped (id or position not on the checklist)
generate.modelRejected: None of the {{dropped}} model row(s) was adopted: {{reason}}
generate.modelFailed: The model leg did not run; fell back to the reorder-only conservative version: {{reason}}
generate.modelUnavailable: No model was used; this run only reorders, it does not rewrite: {{reason}}
generate.modelDisabled: The model leg is switched off in configuration; this run only reorders
generate.receipt: Target résumé {{docId}} · prompt {{prompt}} · retried before check {{retried}}
generate.needsHuman: Needs a human decision: the violation rows below are the checker's readout (path, rule and length only — never the text). Whether to act on them is your call; nothing was written into the working copy.
generate.violationsTruncated: {{total}} violation(s) in total, only the first ones are expanded

generate.sourceNotModeled: This section does not produce entity rows (ruling 4.2-ii); its prose is indexed as a section-level chunk, so no entity id exists here — that is neither a miss nor an unsynced library.
generate.sourceNoVerbatim: This entry does have entity rows, but none of their payload values equals this original text verbatim: no source to cite, confirm it by hand before accepting.
generate.reorderEmpty: Nothing moved: this run did not change any section or entry order.
generate.reorderApply: Adopt the reordering (all {{count}} move(s) at once; there is no per-move rollback)
generate.reorderDisplaced: Nothing in this row matched the JD; it only shifted because more relevant rows moved ahead, and its relative order is unchanged.
generate.selectedCount: {{selected}} of {{total}} ticked: with nothing ticked the accept button stays disabled, because there would be nothing to write
generate.accepted: Written into the working copy: {{applied}} rewrite(s) · {{sections}} section move(s) · {{entries}} entry move(s) · timestamp {{at}}
generate.acceptedRebind: The working copy is now the edited version, while the library's entities and retrieval index still reflect the previous one: re-sync before the next comparison or generation.
generate.errorMissing: That proposal is gone (the service restarted or the retention window passed): generate again before accepting. Nothing was written.
generate.errorStale: You edited this résumé after the generation: stacking the two changes produces something nobody can explain. Generate again from the current version. Nothing was written.
generate.errorCheck: The combination you selected failed the fact check, so nothing was written: {{message}}

model.heading: Model
model.note: This section does three things in one place: keep several providers at once (Volcano Engine, OpenAI and DeepSeek each get a row), fetch each one's model list and tick entries into this machine, then pick one for the chat leg and one for the embeddings leg. Base URL and model name go to the persisted layer under userData, the key goes to the secret store, and the UI only ever shows its last 4 characters.
